headline: A strong storm sweeps in Wednesday evening into Thanksgiving with heavy rain, gusts to 50 mph along the Strait and North Interior and 45 mph around Puget Sound (60 mph on the coast), a foot or more of mountain snow, and more coastal flooding at Thursday morning's high tide.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain fills in along the coast Wednesday afternoon and spreads across the interior this evening as a strong storm front pushes ashore, with gusts already 20 to 30 mph and climbing tonight. A Wind Advisory runs 4 PM Wednesday to noon Thursday for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca, the Lake Crescent/US 101 area, Port Townsend, the San Juans, Whidbey and the north Sound lowlands, where gusts reach about 50 mph; Seattle, the Eastside, Kitsap, Tacoma and Olympia are under a Wind Advisory from 8 PM Wednesday to noon Thursday with gusts to 45 mph, peaking around 2 to 7 AM Thursday in Seattle. The outer coast gets the strongest winds, gusting up to 60 mph, under a High Wind Warning from 8 PM Wednesday to noon Thursday. A Winter Storm Warning covers the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades from 7 PM Wednesday to 4 AM Friday, with 8 to 16 inches possible in the North Cascades mostly tonight into Thursday and snow levels around 5,000 to 6,000 feet.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain turns to showers behind the front on Thanksgiving, and the air turns unstable enough for scattered thunderstorms, with a 20 to 25 percent chance on the coast and Olympic Peninsula and about 15 to 20 percent or less in the interior, mainly late morning into the afternoon. Winds ease through the day (Seattle gusts near 30 mph Thursday afternoon) and die down Thursday evening. Storm totals of 2 to 4 inches through Thursday fall mostly on the Olympic Peninsula and coast; rivers will rise without widespread flooding, except the Skokomish River, which is expected to peak at moderate flood stage late tonight into early Thursday under a River Flood Warning through Friday, and more small landslides are possible on the Bear Gulch burn scar on the Olympic Peninsula. A weaker system keeps rain chances going Friday, though impacts should be minimal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models agree well that weak high pressure builds over the Pacific Northwest late Friday and through the weekend, giving a break from the rain Saturday and Sunday. The stormy pattern returns next week, starting with another system on Monday that brings breezy winds, mainly to the coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

coast: Coastal flooding remains the headline hazard as some of the year's highest tides combine with storm surge and high surf, peaking on the outer coast Wednesday and in the inland waters early Thursday before tides gradually weaken. A Coastal Flood Warning runs until 4 PM Wednesday for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including Port Angeles and Sequim) and the Washington coast, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon for the Strait, Port Townsend and the coast; a Coastal Flood Warning runs 3 AM to 10 AM Thursday for Seattle, Everett, Shoreline/Lynnwood, eastern Kitsap, Island County, northern Hood Canal, the San Juans and the Pierce/south King, Skagit/Snohomish and Whatcom lowlands, and a Coastal Flood Advisory covers the lower Chehalis River valley and the San Juans until 4 PM Wednesday. A High Surf Advisory covers the coast until 4 PM Wednesday. On the water, a Storm Warning covers the coastal waters and Gale Warnings cover the east and west entrances of the Strait, Admiralty Inlet and the northern inland waters and San Juans until 10 AM Thursday, with a Gale Warning for Puget Sound and Hood Canal from midnight to 7 AM Thursday and Small Craft Advisories around those hours, for the central Strait (4 PM Wednesday to 10 PM Thursday), the coastal waters (10 AM to 10 PM Thursday) and the Grays Harbor bar. Thunderstorms over the coastal waters early Thursday may move into the inland waters with lightning, gusty winds and small hail. Seas of 15 to 21 feet continue into Thursday, ease to 10 to 15 feet late Thursday into Friday and below 10 feet over the weekend (with a weak westerly push through the Strait late Saturday into Sunday), then rise above 10 feet again next week, when more advisories are likely.
watch_for: Thursday morning's high tide (3–10 AM), when storm surge adds to coastal flooding along the Strait and Puget Sound
Gusts of 45–60 mph tonight into Thursday morning, strongest on the coast, the Strait and the North Interior
Skokomish River flooding and possible landslides on the Bear Gulch burn scar through Thursday
confidence: Models agree well on the dry weekend break, while the discussion gives few specifics yet on the timing or strength of next week's storms.
